description: Browser-supplied UA string. The single most-checked fingerprint surface.
Structured Client Hints. Newer than userAgent; many spoofers forget to override it, creating a tell.
Standardized boolean that is `true` whenever the browser is driven by WebDriver/CDP. Hard signal of automation.
Plugin list. Headless Chrome has zero by default; legitimate Chrome reports PDF Viewer entries. Empty list is a tell.
Companion to plugins; checked together for consistency.
Locale preference array. Empty array (length 0) was a long-standing headless tell. Mismatch with Accept-Language header is also flagged.
Primary locale. Cross-checked against languages[0], Intl, and Accept-Language.
Logical CPU count. Combined with deviceMemory and timing micro-benchmarks to fingerprint hardware.
Approximate RAM in GB (rounded). Chrome only. Coarse but stable signal.
OS string (Win32, MacIntel, Linux x86_64). Cross-checked with userAgent.
Browser vendor string ('Google Inc.', 'Apple Computer, Inc.', '').
Almost always empty; used in rare consistency checks.
'20030107' on WebKit/Blink, '20100101' on Gecko. A small but exact fingerprint axis.
Firefox-only OS/CPU descriptor; presence on a UA claiming Chrome is a tell.
Firefox build ID; presence outside Firefox is suspicious.
User DNT preference ('1', '0', null, 'unspecified'). Adds entropy.
Boolean; near-universally true in real browsers.
Network connectivity hint.
Touch capability. Headless Chrome on Linux reports 0 even when UA claims mobile — strong inconsistency tell.
Newer Chrome property; should be true on regular Chrome.
NetworkInformation. effectiveType / downlink / rtt are stable per network and used as a fingerprint axis.
Permissions API. The `Notification.permission === 'denied' && permissions.query({name:'notifications'}).state === 'prompt'` mismatch is the canonical Chrome-headless detector.
Service worker registration interface; presence checked for capability.
Media device enumeration. enumerateDevices() returns devices' deviceId/label — strong fingerprint axis.
Battery API (deprecated in many browsers). Charging state, level, and discharge time form a transient fingerprint.
Gamepad enumeration; mostly checked for capability presence.
PWA-related; rarely used for detection.
Bluetooth API capability check.
WebUSB capability check.
WebGPU. Adapter info exposes high-resolution GPU model strings.
StorageManager. estimate() leaks rough disk quota.
Presentation API; rarely fingerprinted.
Legacy UA companion. Detectors cross-check appVersion against userAgent — they normally only differ in the leading 'Mozilla/'.
Always 'Netscape' on real browsers — anomaly is a tell.
Always 'Mozilla' on real browsers.
Always 'Gecko' on real browsers.
GPC signal (true/false/undefined). Adds a small fingerprint axis tied to user privacy settings.
Brave-only namespace. brave.isBrave() / brave.getBraveMode() identify Brave even when UA mimics Chrome. Common evasion target.
App-badge API capability check; rarely fingerprinted directly.
Companion to setAppBadge.
Legacy quota API. queryUsageAndQuota leaks disk quota even when navigator.storage is patched.
Legacy persistent-storage quota API; same axis as webkitTemporaryStorage.
Entry point for MediaCapabilities.decodingInfo / .encodingInfo. Hardware codec support is a strong fingerprint axis.
Brand list (e.g., 'Chromium', 'Google Chrome', 'Not_A Brand'). Mismatch with UA major version is a spoof tell.
Mobile flag. Must be consistent with maxTouchPoints, viewport, and UA.
Platform string (e.g., 'macOS', 'Windows'). Cross-checked with navigator.platform and userAgent.
Async API for platformVersion / architecture / bitness / model / uaFullVersion / wow64. Strong fingerprint axis; missing or inconsistent results vs UA strings flag spoofs.
Aliased high-entropy probe (var d = navigator.userAgentData; d.getHighEntropyValues()).
navigator.gpu.requestAdapter(). Returns a GPUAdapter whose requestAdapterInfo() leaks vendor/architecture/device — a WebGPU-era replacement for WEBGL_debug_renderer_info.
GPUAdapter.requestAdapterInfo(). High-resolution GPU identity for WebGPU. Hooking this is a frequent gap in stealth toolchains.
navigator.bluetooth.getAvailability(). Returns whether a Bluetooth radio is present — a coarse hardware probe.
Web MIDI. Presence and the resolved MIDIAccess.inputs/.outputs list reveal connected MIDI devices.
Media Session API. Capability probe — Chrome mobile leaning signal.
Web Share API. Mobile-Chrome signal; capability check.
Companion to navigator.share.
Contacts API (Android Chrome).
VirtualKeyboard API (Chromium/ChromeOS/Edge).
WakeLock API. .request('screen') secure-context probe.
Web Serial (Chromium-only).
WebHID (Chromium-only).
Web Locks API.
Chromium-only navigator.scheduling.isInputPending(). Presence pins Blink.
Clipboard API root. readText/writeText permission-gated; presence/absence and permission state are fingerprint axes.
UserActivation v2. .hasBeenActive and .isActive. False throughout the session = automation that never produced a real user gesture.
Aliased userActivation access.
navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia. Desktop-only — absence on a Chrome-desktop UA is a tell.
Legacy VR enumeration; Firefox-only. Presence reveals engine.
Legacy VR enumeration.
Legacy IE/Edge surface; presence in modern Chrome would be a spoofer artifact.
Common fingerprint-exfiltration sink used by ebay/microsoft/stackoverflow/washingtonpost trackers (EssentialFP 2020). Listed here because the call signals 'tracker' even when the body is opaque.

Vibration API. Presence/behavior varies by platform (no-op on desktop, gated on mobile); a long-standing device-class tell ('Most Websites Don't Need to Vibrate', 2017). Automation often mismatches the expected platform behavior.
PWA window-controls-overlay surface. Present in Chromium; its .visible state / getTitlebarAreaRect() is an installed-PWA / display-mode tell that headless contexts get wrong.
WebXR entry point. Presence and xr.isSessionSupported() responses form a feature-detection tell; absent in many headless builds.
Physical display width in CSS pixels.
Physical display height in CSS pixels.
Available width minus OS chrome (taskbar, dock).
Available height minus OS chrome.
Almost always 24. Anomalous values (e.g., 48) are headless tells.
Mirrors colorDepth. Mismatch is suspicious.
Orientation type/angle — mostly mobile detection.
Viewport width. Combined with outer dimensions to detect headless (outer often 0 in headless).
Viewport height.
Window-frame width. 0 in headless Chrome — a very common tell.
Window-frame height. 0 in headless — common tell.
DPR; values like 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3 are common. Combined with screen size.
Real Chrome exposes `window.chrome` with .runtime, .app, .csi, .loadTimes. Headless Chrome historically lacked it; Puppeteer-extra-stealth restores it. Still probed for sub-property correctness.

Chrome extension runtime. Presence on a non-extension page is normal; absence is a headless tell. Also the entry point for extension-fingerprinting probes via chrome.runtime.sendMessage / .connect against known extension IDs (Carnus 2020).
Deprecated but still probed. Calling it should return an object with specific fields.
Deprecated client-side instrumentation. Existence is checked.
Legacy Opera detection.
Often 1 in fresh automated sessions; non-1 suggests real navigation.
Current URL; trivially checked.
X position of available screen area. Non-zero on macOS (menu bar offset) — used as OS hint.
Y position of available screen area. Non-zero on Windows (taskbar top) or macOS (menu bar).
Window's screen X. 0 in headless; non-zero in real browsers when window isn't full-screen.
Window's screen Y; same axis as screenX.
Older alias of screenX in some browsers.
Older alias of screenY.
VisualViewport. width/height/scale. When visualViewport.width === screen.width, the page is likely running headless / pinned-tab fullscreen.
Aliased visualViewport access (var v = window.visualViewport).
File System Access API. Chrome-desktop only — absence on a Chrome-desktop UA is a tell.
File System Access API directory picker; same Chrome-desktop signal.
File System Access API save dialog.
Firefox-only object; presence pins Gecko engine even when UA spoofed.
Window.frames live list. window.frames.length and window.top !== window.self are used to detect iframed contexts.
Persistent across same-tab navigations; used by some trackers to bridge identity across origins.
Boolean reflecting COOP+COEP. Required for SharedArrayBuffer in modern browsers — its value cross-checks the environment with the SharedArrayBuffer availability tell.
Multi-screen Window Management API. Presence pins Chrome 100+; getScreenDetails() returns per-display geometry.
window.getScreenDetails(). Permission-gated multi-monitor probe.
Cookie jar access. Checked for presence and for specific anti-bot cookies (Akamai _abck, Cloudflare cf_clearance, DataDome).
Referring URL. Empty on direct nav; checked alongside Referer header.
Page Visibility API; false in foreground tabs.
Companion to .hidden ('visible'/'hidden'/'prerender').
True if document has focus. Headless windows often lack focus events.
Document character encoding.
Root element; typical entry point for client-rect / layout fingerprinting.
Body element; sometimes attribute-checked for automation tells.
Used to construct probe elements (canvas, audio, video) for fingerprinting.
FontFaceSet. Detectors enumerate, call check()/load() on probe families to fingerprint installed fonts.
DOMImplementation; rarely fingerprinted.
Live StyleSheetList. Iterating + reading .cssRules exposes the engine's CSS-property normalization (shorthand expansion order, default values).
Reference to the executing <script> element. Detectors read .src and fetch the URL back to verify byte-for-byte integrity of their loaded blob.
Namespaced element creation. Common for SVG fingerprint probes (createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text')).
Range constructor. Range.getBoundingClientRect of a selected text node is a font-fingerprint path that bypasses canvas hooks.
DocumentTimeline.currentTime. Subtle high-resolution clock alternative to performance.now().
Legacy event factory. createEvent('TouchEvent') is a touch-capability probe that throws on non-touch browsers.

HTMLIFrameElement.contentWindow. Detectors create a hidden iframe and re-read navigator.webdriver / window.chrome / Notification.permission from the iframe's pristine realm — bypasses main-window patches.
Same cross-realm escape hatch as contentWindow.
Async cookie API constructor — capability probe (Chrome 87+).
Global async cookie API. get/getAll bypass document.cookie strict-domain rules.
Document.adoptedStyleSheets. Live list of constructable stylesheets attached to the document. Extension-injected styles often appear here even when hidden from document.styleSheets.
ShadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets; same axis.
Acquires a 2D canvas context — almost always a prelude to canvas fingerprinting.
Serializes a canvas to a base64 PNG/JPEG. The most common canvas-fingerprinting sink.
Async sibling of toDataURL — identical fingerprint risk.
Reads pixel data directly. Bypasses toDataURL hooks; intercept here too if defending.
Fingerprinting scripts paint a known glyph string and read pixels back. fillText use near getImageData/toDataURL is the canonical pattern.
Companion to fillText; rasterization differences across font stacks/GPUs leak entropy.
Returns a TextMetrics. Width and bounding-box numbers vary per font and system.
Used in some uncommon canvas probes.
Allocates a blank ImageData buffer.
Writes pixels back to a canvas.
Path construction; not fingerprint-critical on its own.
Path construction; sometimes used in canvas probes.
Fills the current path.
Strokes the current path.
Fills a rectangle. Appears as part of canvas fingerprint setup (background).
Clears a rectangle.
Path move; common in canvas fingerprint test images.
Path line; canvas fingerprint setup.
Path ellipse; part of canvas-fingerprint shape suites.
Path bezier; rare outside canvas-fingerprint test images.
Path quadratic; rare outside canvas-fingerprint test images.
Radial gradient; commonly used in canvas-fingerprint setup to elicit GPU-blend variance.
Linear gradient; same fingerprint role as createRadialGradient.
Gradient stop; appears with createRadialGradient/createLinearGradient.
TextMetrics.actualBoundingBoxAscent. Sub-pixel glyph metric exposed via measureText(). Strong font-render fingerprint.
TextMetrics.actualBoundingBoxDescent. Same axis as ascent.
TextMetrics.actualBoundingBoxLeft.
TextMetrics.actualBoundingBoxRight.
TextMetrics.fontBoundingBoxAscent — font-level metric (vs glyph-level).
TextMetrics.fontBoundingBoxDescent.
Acquires a WebGL/WebGPU context — gateway for GPU fingerprinting.
Reads named parameters from a WebGL context. Heavily used for VENDOR/RENDERER + many capability ints.
Requests the debug-renderer-info extension which unlocks UNMASKED_VENDOR_WEBGL (37445) and UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL (37446) — the GPU model string.
General extension query. Detectors also enumerate via getSupportedExtensions().
Returns the list of WebGL extensions the GPU/driver supports — high-entropy fingerprint axis.
Returns precision range/precision for shader types. Stable per GPU.
Returns the attributes the context was created with.
Reads pixels back from a rendered scene — used to fingerprint shader output.
Uploads GLSL source. Appearance of long shader source near readPixels indicates a render-output fingerprint (DRAWNAPART-style probes).
Compiles a shader. Common in GPU-fingerprint pipelines.
Links a shader program. Step in WebGL fingerprint setup.
Activates a linked program.
Issues a draw call. Paired with readPixels to extract GPU output for fingerprinting.
Indexed draw call; same fingerprint role as drawArrays.
Uploads vertex/index data; standard WebGL setup.
Binds a buffer.
Allocates a shader object.
Allocates a program object.
Resolves attribute index.
Resolves uniform location.
Vertex attribute setup.
WebGL viewport set; appears in fingerprint render setup.

Disjoint Timer Query extension. Unlocks gl.createQuery / beginQuery / endQuery / getQueryParameter for GPU-side nanosecond timing — the DRAWNAPART (2022) attack uses this to fingerprint GPU stalls below the WebGL renderer string.
Required by DRAWNAPART; presence reveals ANGLE wrapper (Windows Chrome).
Compressed-texture extension probe. Set varies by GPU class (mobile/desktop, NVIDIA/AMD/Intel/Mali/Adreno).
WebGL2 Query object; with TIME_ELAPSED_EXT counts GPU nanoseconds. Core primitive in DRAWNAPART-style timing fingerprints.
Starts a timer query — DRAWNAPART pattern.
Ends a timer query — DRAWNAPART pattern.
Reads QUERY_RESULT — GPU-side nanosecond timing exfiltrated to a fingerprint.
Integer uniform set. Appears en-masse in DRAWNAPART pattern (per-iteration uniform updates).
WebGL2 transform feedback. Captures vertex-shader output without rendering — alternate fingerprint-extraction path.
Begins transform-feedback capture.
Web Audio API entry point. Combined with OfflineAudioContext for the canonical audio fingerprint.
Renders audio offline at full speed. Standard fingerprinting recipe: oscillator → compressor → render → hash output buffer.
Legacy prefixed AudioContext — detectors often probe both.
Creates an OscillatorNode — the source signal in audio fingerprinting.
DynamicsCompressorNode — its quirky DSP behaviour across CPU/OS combinations is the entropy source.
AnalyserNode for frequency/time-domain reads.
Reads raw PCM samples — the read-side of the audio fingerprint pipeline.
Spectral output read; alternative read sink.
OfflineAudioContext.startRendering — kicks off the offline render whose output is hashed.
BiquadFilterNode. Default values (frequency.defaultValue, Q.defaultValue, gain.maxValue) are stable per-engine and form an audio-fingerprint axis.
GainNode constructor.
AudioBufferSourceNode; alternative signal source.
ScriptProcessorNode — deprecated but still functional for per-sample fingerprinting.
AnalyserNode.getByteFrequencyData — alternative spectral read.
AnalyserNode.getByteTimeDomainData — time-domain read.
AnalyserNode.getFloatTimeDomainData — float time-domain read.
AudioBuffer.copyFromChannel. Alternative pixel-equivalent read for audio buffer; stealth shims patching getChannelData often forget this path.
AudioBuffer.copyToChannel; less common but still fingerprint-relevant.
AudioContext.baseLatency. Float that depends on the OS audio stack (e.g. 0.01160997… on Linux/44.1kHz). Strong OS-fingerprint axis used by 2022 AudioContext Browser Fingerprinting.
AudioContext.outputLatency. Nonzero on hardware contexts; 0 on offline. Helps separate live-audio from offline fingerprint paths.
AudioContext.sampleRate. 44100 on Linux defaults, 48000 on macOS — coarse OS hint.
AudioContext.destination.maxChannelCount. 2/6/8 distinguishes stereo / 5.1 / 7.1 audio hardware.
Modern audio-processing worklet; presence pins Chrome 66+.
AudioWorklet node constructor.
AudioWorklet.addModule(). Used to load a custom AudioWorkletProcessor; processing latency leaks CPU class.
WebRTC entry point. Used both for STUN-based local-IP leaks and to fingerprint the codec list (SDP).
Legacy prefixed WebRTC.
Firefox-prefixed legacy WebRTC.
Cheap way to force ICE candidate gathering without needing media permissions.
Initiates SDP offer; SDP body contains codec/extension fingerprint material.
Triggers ICE gathering — the step that surfaces local IP candidates.
SDP wrapper; rarely the focus on its own.
Candidate parsing; presence near a regex over `candidate:` lines indicates IP leak harvesting.
RTCPeerConnection.createAnswer. SDP answer body contains codec/extension fingerprint material.
Counterpart to setLocalDescription; rarely the fingerprint target on its own.
RTCRtpSender.getCapabilities('video'/'audio') returns codecs/headerExtensions/fec without ever instantiating a connection — a fast, low-noise codec-fingerprint surface that bypasses SDP harvesting.
Sibling of RTCRtpSender.getCapabilities; same codec/extension fingerprint axis from the receive side.
Capability probe — presence pins WebRTC unified-plan support.
Aliased static-capability probe (var s = RTCRtpSender; s.getCapabilities('video')).

RTCPeerConnection.onicecandidate handler. THE IP-leak hook: the callback receives ICE candidates including local IP addresses parseable from the SDP candidate line. Read or assignment both worth flagging.
RTCPeerConnection.addIceCandidate. Less common as a leak vector, but appears in symmetric setups that round-trip candidates.

RTCPeerConnection.localDescription. SDP body containing every gathered ICE candidate (including local-IP host candidates). Reading the .sdp string and regex-scanning for `candidate:` lines is the standard IP-leak harvest.
RTCIceCandidate.candidate. The raw SDP candidate line — contains the local IP. Reading this near a regex over /^candidate:/ is the IP-extraction signature.
RTCPeerConnection.iceGatheringState ('new' | 'gathering' | 'complete'). Polled during IP-leak harvesting to know when to read localDescription.
Sibling of iceGatheringState; less commonly load-bearing for fingerprinting.

RTCPeerConnection.getStats(). Returns the WebRTC stats dictionary — RTT, jitter, congestion-window samples. Used in 2014/2020 Markov-chain encrypted-traffic-classification work and by some advanced detectors to fingerprint the local network path.

RTCDataChannel constructor reference. Detectors create one to force ICE gathering without media permissions; the channel itself is also a *peer-to-peer exfil sink* that bypasses the conventional fetch/XHR/sendBeacon enumeration.

Generic *.send — fires for WebSocket.send, RTCDataChannel.send, and others. Treat in context: alone it's noisy; in combination with RTCPeerConnection construction it's a P2P exfil sink not visible to the normal HTTP-sink enumeration.
RTCDataChannel.bufferedAmount / WebSocket.bufferedAmount. Backpressure probe.

RTCSessionDescription.sdp. The full SDP text containing every codec, header extension, and ICE candidate the offer/answer expressed. High-entropy fingerprint axis — the codec ordering alone can pin a UA's actual engine version.
Static enumeration of supported send codecs / header-extensions. Codec list and ordering are an engine/OS fingerprint axis available without ever constructing a peer connection.
Static enumeration of supported receive codecs / header-extensions. Paired with the sender capabilities for a high-entropy, instance-free WebRTC codec fingerprint.
High-resolution clock. Used both for timing micro-benchmarks (cache, JIT, GC behaviour) and to detect breakpoints (huge gaps).
Deprecated navigation timing object.
Origin of performance.now() timestamps. Together with Date.now they let detectors verify timer monotonicity / detect clock skew.
Chrome-only heap stats (jsHeapSizeLimit, totalJSHeapSize, usedJSHeapSize). Stable per-platform; absence on a Chrome UA is a tell.
Resource timing entries — used to confirm that expected page resources actually loaded.
Filtered resource timing.
Wall-clock millis. Compared against performance.now to detect time desync.
Timezone offset in minutes. Cross-checked with Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone and Accept-Language hints.
Date constructor. new Date().toString() exposes the locale-aware TZ abbreviation (e.g., 'GMT-0800 (Pacific Standard Time)') — a cheap TZ tell distinct from Intl.DateTimeFormat.
Date parser; rarely fingerprinted.
Yields locale-aware long-form timezone abbreviation. Detectors regex-extract the parenthesized TZ name (e.g., 'Pacific Standard Time') and cross-check with Intl.DateTimeFormat.
Date getter; common in DST winter/summer offset probes.
Frame-cadence access. Detectors measure callback intervals to detect off-screen / headless rendering (no display = irregular cadence).
performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory(). Chrome-only (cross-origin-isolated context). Exposes per-context memory class — both a UA tell and a finer alternative to performance.memory.
resolvedOptions().timeZone leaks the IANA timezone string. format()/formatToParts() outputs vary across ICU builds (Chrome vs Node vs Firefox).
resolvedOptions().locale + format() output (currency symbol position, decimal separator) leaks ICU locale. Compact-notation strings vary across versions.
Locale-aware comparison. compare() ordering of edge-case strings reveals the underlying ICU collation table.
of(code) returns localized language/region/script names. Used as a high-signal locale-system axis — different platforms ship different display-name tables.
format([...]) joins items with locale-specific separators ('and'/','/' und '/etc.). Output varies across ICU versions.
select(n) returns the plural form ('one'/'few'/'many'/'other') for a locale. Subtle cross-platform differences for less-common locales.
format(value, unit) returns 'in 3 days', 'next year', etc. Strong locale-system fingerprint axis.
Locale tag parser. Constructor + resolvedOptions exposes default calendar/numbering system/case-first behaviour.
Grapheme/word/sentence segmentation. Different ICU builds segment emoji ZWJ sequences differently — a tell for Chromium vs WebKit vs Gecko.
Universal Intl.* method that exposes the resolved locale tag, timezone, calendar, numbering system, and per-formatter defaults. Heavy on the Intl.X.resolvedOptions() pattern in fingerprinters.
Structured formatter output. Detectors compare specific parts (literal separators, currency placement) across locales rather than the whole string.
PhantomJS bridge function. Existence on `window` proves PhantomJS.
PhantomJS internal handle.
Older PhantomJS marker.
Node.js Buffer leaking into a 'browser' context — signals a Node-based driver (Electron, NW.js, Nightmare).
EventEmitter-style global; classic Nightmare/Electron leak.
Node child_process leak.
Chrome --enable-automation injects this. Direct tell.
Chrome --enable-automation injects this. Direct tell.
Nightmare.js bridge.
Selenium IDE marker.
Selenium internal property.
Selenium internal property.
Selenium injected helper.
Selenium injected helper.
Selenium injected helper.
Firefox driver helper.
Selenium driver-unwrapped marker.
Selenium driver-unwrapped marker.
Selenium evaluator helper.
Firefox driver helper.
ChromeDriver injects this property on document. The exact name is hardcoded in chromedriver.exe binaries; patching the binary is one mitigation.
ChromeDriver async-script bridge marker.
ChromeDriver-injected sentinel; same family as $cdc_.
ChromeDriver-injected sentinel.
ChromeDriver-injected sentinel.
Probes the prototype chain to bypass instance-level shims.
Playwright binding marker injected into pages with exposed bindings.
Playwright init-script bookkeeping global.
Puppeteer source-name marker in stack traces.
Selenium-IDE injected sentinel.
Selenium-IDE recorder marker.
Selenium browser-driver capitalized marker.
Bare `webdriver` global on `window` — appears in some configurations beyond the navigator property.
Node-process global leaking into a browser realm (Electron, NW.js, jsdom).
Node `require` leaking into a browser realm.
Node `module` leaking; weaker signal because some bundlers create it intentionally.
Node `global` leaking. Often paired with `process` checks.
Reading outerHeight on the prototype side-steps instance-level overrides; 0 confirms headless.

DevTools command-line API helper. Only defined when evaluation runs with includeCommandLineAPI (CDP Runtime.evaluate). A defined `getEventListeners` in page scope betrays a CDP/automation evaluation context (StableBrowse, 'reading challenge scripts').

Source-of-function probe. Detectors call .toString() on patched native methods (e.g., navigator.permissions.query) and check it returns `function name() { [native code] }`. Monkey-patches that don't impersonate native source are flagged.
Generic .toString call — could be the function probe above or could be benign string conversion.
Reads property descriptors. Used to detect getter overrides (a getter that wasn't there before) and to verify [[Configurable]] / [[Writable]] match real-Chrome shape.
Bulk descriptor read.
Enumerates own properties; used to find injected helper props.
Walks prototype chain — common in webdriver-prototype probes.
Often appears in BOTH detection (locking properties) and evasion (overriding getters). Presence isn't a tell on its own; descriptor argument shape matters.
Like getOwnPropertyNames + getOwnPropertySymbols.
Proxies are heavily used by stealth shims; detectors test for Proxy traces (e.g., toString of trapped functions).
Used in deep type-coercion probes.
Walks back to a function from an instance. Check `obj.constructor.name` for class name.
Direct prototype access. Often paired with webdriver detection.
V8-specific. Stack-trace contents leak the engine and frame names.
V8 hook for structured stack traces. Some detectors install one to inspect call sites and detect Puppeteer/Playwright glue frames.
Indirect property read. Stealth-bypass technique used by detectors to dodge Object.defineProperty-style getter overrides on common APIs.
Same descriptor read as Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor; alternative entry point.
in-operator equivalent. Rarely fingerprint-load-bearing on its own.
Used alongside Proxy in anti-fp shim detection.
Prototype walk via Reflect; same axis as Object.getPrototypeOf.
Property removal probe — used to check whether a property is [[Configurable]].
Prototype reassignment. Stealth shims sometimes use this; detectors probe for traces.
Object factory. Used in lie-detection cycles (Object.create with cyclic prototype to trigger engine-specific TypeError).
Standard property probe. Slightly elevated because lie-detection scripts use it to test that webdriver/permissions properties exist on the right object.
Custom instanceof hook. Trapped Proxies that expose Symbol.hasInstance trip lie-detection.
Iterator protocol; rarely the focus.
Async iterator protocol; rarely the focus.
Class brand tag. Detectors check `Object.prototype.toString.call(navigator.permissions)` returns '[object Permissions]'; tampered prototypes leak the tag.
`eval.toString().length` is a stable engine signature: 33 on V8, 37 on SpiderMonkey, 37 on JSC. Spoofed-UA detection compares this with the claimed browser engine.

Legacy setter introspection. Shape Shifter and other anti-anti-fp tools use `Object.__lookupSetter__('foo').toString()` to detect monkey-patched setters that Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor might miss.
Legacy getter introspection. Same anti-stealth role.

Double-toString trick to defeat naïve Function.prototype.toString patches. If the override of toString itself isn't shadowed, this returns the patched source — strong tell for AntiDetect-style wrappers.

Stack-trace text read (typically `new Error().stack` or `e.stack` in a catch). Detectors regex this for framework-glue frames: `__puppeteer_evaluation_script__`, `pptr://`, `playwright`, `chrome-extension://`, anonymous frames matching CDP's evaluate pattern. Pair with `Error.prepareStackTrace` for V8-only structured access.
Bind on Function.prototype. Often paired with .toString to verify a bound function still serializes as native code — stealth wrappers that forget to mask the bound-version source are caught here.
Function.prototype.call. Common in indirect-invocation introspection probes (`Function.prototype.call.toString()` length check).
Function.prototype.apply. Same axis as .call.

`Function.toString.call(victim)` is the classic stealth-bypass trampoline: it sidesteps a patched `Function.prototype.toString` by calling the constructor's own .toString directly. If a wrapper masks the prototype but not Function itself, this returns the unmasked source.

Variant of the constructor-trampoline: `(navigator.permissions.query).constructor.toString.call(victim)` reaches Function.prototype.toString through the constructor chain. Catches patches that only shadow Function.prototype.
V8-specific stack-trace depth cap. Reads/writes here are usually scaffolding for a deeper stack probe — flag for context.
Persistent key/value store. Detectors stash device IDs / risk scores here for cross-session correlation.
Tab-scoped storage; sometimes used to hold per-session detection state.
Larger persistent store; detectors use it for evercookies / device IDs.
Deprecated WebSQL. Capability presence still occasionally used.
navigator.storage.estimate() leaks rough disk quota — coarse but stable.
Programmatic font registration; unusual outside fingerprinters.
document.fonts.check('12px Foo') tests a probe family — efficient font enumeration.
document.fonts.load(); used both for font fingerprinting and benign loading.
indexedDB.databases(). Returns names of existing DBs — leaks 'returning visitor' status without a cookie.
CacheStorage root. Same returning-visitor leak via caches.keys().
caches.keys() (when on CacheStorage). Lists installed PWA caches.
Constructor; rarely invoked directly but referenced in prototype probes.
caches.open(name). Opens a named Cache. Re-using a known name across visits is the most common SW-based persistent identifier.
caches.match(req) / cache.match(req). Read path — used by SW-based trackers to check whether a per-visitor cache entry already exists (returning-visitor signal).
cache.put(req, res). Stores a per-visitor response; combined with caches.match, the canonical evercookie path inside a SW.
caches.delete / cache.delete. Removal probe; rarely fingerprint-load-bearing on its own.
caches.has(name). Existence probe — cheaper than open() for returning-visitor detection.

BroadcastChannel constructor. Used by SW-based cross-tab tracking to coordinate session-state without storage events. Presence in a fingerprint blob is suspicious because there's no benign reason for a detector to need cross-tab messaging.
MessagePort/BroadcastChannel/Window.postMessage. Cross-realm exfiltration channel — Botguard's PO-Token flow uses this to push attested tokens to a hidden iframe before they get sent over the wire.
Constructor reference. Detectors usually receive a registration from navigator.serviceWorker.register, not by constructing one.
navigator.serviceWorker.controller. Non-null means a SW is already controlling the page — returning-visitor / persistent-session tell.
ServiceWorkerRegistration.scope. Reveals the URL pattern the SW controls.
navigator.serviceWorker.ready. Awaitable that resolves once the active SW is in control.

Local Font Access API (window.queryLocalFonts). Permission-gated enumeration of the full installed font set — extremely high entropy. Presence of the API and the granted/denied/empty result are all tells; headless has no real font set.
Capability check. Headless desktop browsers expose it but never fire; mobile-claiming UAs that don't fire DeviceMotion are flagged.
Same family as DeviceMotionEvent — expected to fire on real mobile.
Touch capability check. Combined with maxTouchPoints and pointer media-queries.
Pointer event capability.
Generic Sensor API class. Modern but rarely fingerprinted alone.
Generic Sensor API class.
Behind feature flag in most browsers.
Generic Sensor API class; constructor presence is a capability probe.
Generic Sensor API class.
Generic Sensor API class.
Generic Sensor API class.
Generic Sensor API class.
Base class presence check.
navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices(). Returns device entries (kind, deviceId, groupId, label). Empty array or default-only labels signal headless.
Capability check; rarely actually invoked by detectors.
HTMLMediaElement.canPlayType. Returns 'probably' / 'maybe' / '' across codecs — codec-support fingerprint.
MediaRecorder/MediaSource.isTypeSupported. Codec-support fingerprint axis.
navigator.permissions.query({name:...}). When name is 'notifications', the result is the canonical Chrome-headless detector (Notification.permission='denied' but state='prompt' on headless).
Notification permission state ('default'/'granted'/'denied'). Combined with permissions.query for the headless tell.
CSPRNG; ubiquitous — appears in plenty of legitimate code.
WebCrypto subtle interface; rarely fingerprinted.
Capability check; presence on a UA claiming an old browser is a tell.
navigator.mediaCapabilities root.
navigator.mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo({...}). Returns {supported, smooth, powerEfficient} per codec/resolution. powerEfficient is a strong hardware-decode-availability fingerprint.
navigator.mediaCapabilities.encodingInfo({...}). Hardware-encode capability surface.
MediaSource constructor / static methods. .isTypeSupported is in media-permissions; the constructor presence itself is a capability probe.
Static codec probe — independent of an instance. Detectors enumerate ~30 codec strings (vp9, av01, hvc1, hev1, mp4a.40.x, opus, ec-3) for OS-fingerprint.
Static codec probe for recording. Smaller variation than MediaSource but still a fingerprint axis.

WebCodecs static probe — VideoEncoder/VideoDecoder/AudioEncoder/AudioDecoder.isConfigSupported(). Enumerates hardware/software codec support and acceleration, a GPU/OS-class fingerprint independent of any media element.
Generic listener install. Fingerprint-relevant when the event name is 'mousemove', 'mousedown', 'pointermove', 'devicemotion', or 'deviceorientation' — used to score human-like input.
Synthetic event dispatch. Detectors check `event.isTrusted` — synthetic events are flagged.
Geometry probe. Sub-pixel rect values vary across font-stack/zoom/DPR combinations and are stable per environment.
Multi-rect geometry probe; same fingerprint axis as getBoundingClientRect.
Used both by detectors (to spot late DOM tampering) and by stealth shims (to re-apply patches).
Media-query probes. `(prefers-color-scheme)`, `(prefers-reduced-motion)`, `(forced-colors)`, `(any-pointer)`, `(hover)` all add fingerprint entropy.
Constructor capability probe.
Constructor capability probe.
Constructor capability probe — paired with observe('longtask', 'paint', 'measure').
Brave-resistance fingerprint axis (Brave / Tor return null for new ReportingObserver options).
Generic .observe() call; alone not meaningful, but co-occurrence with PerformanceObserver near timing fingerprints is.
Event.isTrusted. Synthetic events dispatched via dispatchEvent or CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent (without untrusted=false) read as false — direct automation tell.
MouseEvent.movementX. Distribution of mouse-movement deltas; bots produce straight-line / constant-velocity tracks that classifiers separate from human noise.
MouseEvent.movementY.
PointerEvent.pressure. Touch/pen events should report sub-1 values; mouse always 0.5. Constant or NaN under headless automation.
PointerEvent.tangentialPressure. Always 0 unless a real pen is in use.
PointerEvent.tiltX. Pen tilt; 0 unless real input.
PointerEvent.tiltY.
Event.timeStamp. Inter-event delta histogram — bots produce uniform deltas, humans don't.
document.elementFromPoint(x,y). Honeypot-link probing: detectors hide an invisible anchor at known coords; if elementFromPoint returns it AND a click event ever fires on it, the visitor is a bot.
document.elementsFromPoint(x,y). Same honeypot vector as elementFromPoint.
KeyboardEvent.key. Logical key value (e.g. 'a', 'Shift'). Inputs to keystroke-dynamics classifiers.
KeyboardEvent.code. Physical key identifier ('KeyA', 'ShiftLeft'). Inconsistency between .key and .code distribution distinguishes keyboard layouts and detects programmatic dispatch.
KeyboardEvent.repeat. True when the OS is auto-repeating a held key. Synthetic typers (CDP, robotjs) almost never set this — constant `false` across a long key sequence is a tell.
KeyboardEvent.location (0-3 = standard / left / right / numpad). Used to fingerprint physical keyboard layout via shift-side preference in detected sequences.
KeyboardEvent.isComposing / InputEvent.isComposing. Pins IME usage — locale + platform tell.
Legacy KeyboardEvent.charCode. Reads through deprecated path; some old detectors still rely on it.
Legacy KeyboardEvent.keyCode. Same axis as .charCode.
WheelEvent.deltaX. Scroll-velocity profile across multi-event sequences. Constant deltas → synthetic scroll.
WheelEvent.deltaY. Same axis as deltaX.
WheelEvent.deltaZ. Rarely populated; reading it is usually scaffolding for a fuller wheel-fingerprint pass.
WheelEvent.deltaMode (0 = pixel, 1 = line, 2 = page). Trackpad vs mousewheel vs OS-level scroll source — coarse hardware tell.
InputEvent.inputType ('insertText', 'insertCompositionText', 'deleteContentBackward', …). Inferred typing modality (autocomplete, paste, IME) — discriminates programmatic value-set from real typing.
InputEvent.data. The composed text fragment. Often paired with .inputType for IME / paste analysis.

PointerEvent.pointerType ('mouse' | 'pen' | 'touch'). Cross-checked with navigator.maxTouchPoints, userAgentData.mobile, and TouchEvent presence — common consistency-failure axis for headless setups claiming a mobile UA.
PointerEvent.pointerId. Multi-touch session identity; rarely a tell on its own.

Event.composedPath(). Returns the propagation path including shadow-DOM ancestry. Synthetic events dispatched via dispatchEvent without a real target reveal themselves through an unexpected path shape — pair with .isTrusted for the strongest signal.
KeyboardEvent.getModifierState / MouseEvent.getModifierState. Reads lock states (NumLock, CapsLock, ScrollLock) that bot drivers can't easily fake without OS-level injection.
MouseEvent.screenX. Absolute screen-space cursor coords (vs clientX/Y for viewport-space). Distribution + drift over a session input mouse-kinematics models (BeCAPTCHA-Mouse, 2020).
MouseEvent.screenY. Same axis as screenX.
MouseEvent.clientX. Viewport-relative cursor coords; weakly load-bearing alone, strongly load-bearing as a kinematic-trace input.
MouseEvent.clientY. Same as clientX.
Web Speech API root. Mere access is benign but is the gateway to getVoices() — one of the strongest OS-fingerprint surfaces.
Returns the array of SpeechSynthesisVoice. Length, voiceURI prefixes (com.apple.voice.* / Microsoft / native), default flags, and lang tags identify the OS+browser combo.
Aliased speechSynthesis.getVoices receiver. Catches `var s = speechSynthesis; s.getVoices()` patterns the analyzer may not chain through.
Event fired when async voice list resolves. Real Chrome fires once; headless never fires.
Voice class constructor; checked for existence on the global.
Utterance constructor; rarely fingerprinted on its own.
Inverse-cosine precision varies across engines. Common probe input.
Inverse hyperbolic cosine. Fingerprint axis.
Inverse sine. Last-ULP differences across engines.
Inverse hyperbolic sine.
Inverse tangent. A staple math-fingerprint input.
Inverse hyperbolic tangent. Strong cross-engine signal.
Two-arg arctangent. Precision varies.
Cube root.
Cosine. Extreme inputs (e.g., cos(1e308)) reveal engine.
Hyperbolic cosine.
Exponential. Edge-case precision differences.
exp(x) - 1. Different rounding across engines.
Natural log. Precision varies.
log(1+x). Strong precision fingerprint for small x.
Base-10 logarithm.
Base-2 logarithm.
Sine. Extreme inputs are diagnostic.
Hyperbolic sine.
Square root. Usually IEEE-correct everywhere; included for completeness.
Tangent. `Math.tan(-1e300)` is a Tor-precision tell.
Hyperbolic tangent.
sqrt(sum of squares). Implementation differences in overflow handling.
Exponentiation. Last-ULP differences across engines.
Round to nearest float32. Usually IEEE-correct.

window.getComputedStyle(element). Iterating the returned CSSStyleDeclaration enumerates every supported CSS property — strong browser-version fingerprint. Also used for font-presence inference without canvas.
Same surface, accessed via aliased receiver (var gcs = getComputedStyle).
Feature-detection sieve. A bulk CSS.supports() probe over ~50 properties pins the browser engine and version.
CSS selector escaping; rarely fingerprinted.
Constructor feature probe (constructable stylesheets — Chrome 73+).
Element.matches(selector). Used in selector-fingerprint probes (CSS extension detection via :has() + custom selectors).
CSSStyleDeclaration.getPropertyValue. Used by extension-fingerprinting probes to read CSS custom-property values that an extension's content script might inject.
CSSStyleDeclaration.inlineSize. Sub-pixel logical-axis width of a rendered text node — alternative font-metric path that doesn't touch canvas. Used for emoji width fingerprints.
CSSStyleDeclaration.blockSize. Companion to inlineSize.
SVGGraphicsElement.getBBox(). Returns SVGRect with sub-pixel x/y/width/height — strong font-metrics fingerprint that bypasses canvas hooks.
SVGTextContentElement.getComputedTextLength(). Floating-point pixel length of rendered text — per-system, per-font-stack.
SVGTextContentElement.getSubStringLength(). Length of an arbitrary substring; adds entropy beyond getComputedTextLength.
SVGTextContentElement.getExtentOfChar(). Per-glyph bbox; used in glyph-grid font probes.
Char count; usually trivial.
Per-glyph x/y; another font-metric leak.
SVGRect constructor — sometimes referenced via prototype chains in cross-realm probes.
Dedicated Worker constructor. Frequently used by detectors to re-probe navigator/Intl from an unpatched realm.
Cross-tab worker. Same dual-realm fingerprint risk as Worker; less commonly hooked.
ServiceWorker interface; capability probe.
navigator.serviceWorker. .register / .ready / .controller form an exfiltration / persistence axis.

navigator.serviceWorker.register(url). Installs a SW — the persistence-vector entry point (2020 Awakening the Web's Sleeper Agents). The URL also leaks the SW script name, which detectors use for cache-key derivation; SWs outlive the page and continue probing in the background.
WorkerGlobalScope.importScripts. Used to load additional detection logic inside a worker context.
Worker-side canvas constructor. getContext('webgl') on an OffscreenCanvas inside a Worker reveals the GPU even when main-thread getParameter is patched.
Worker-scope navigator. Detectors compare WorkerNavigator.userAgent / .platform / .hardwareConcurrency / .deviceMemory / .languages with main-thread values; mismatch = spoof.
Blob constructor. fingerprinters build worker source as a Blob + URL.createObjectURL to dodge cross-origin script restrictions.
Companion to Blob; URL for the worker source.
Root namespace; capability check.
Compiles a wasm module from bytes. Used in CPU-timing fingerprints.
Streaming compile from a Response. Browser-version probe.
Compile + instantiate. Tight inner loops within the instance leak CPU model.
Streaming instantiate.
Validates wasm bytes without compiling.
Module constructor. Module.imports / Module.exports introspection.
Memory constructor. .shared flag presence identifies cross-origin-isolated context.
Function table constructor.
Global value constructor.
Exception-handling proposal. Presence = Chrome 95+ / Firefox 100+.
WebAssembly.Memory.grow(). The cost of growing memory exposes page-size and TLB behaviour — 16KB pages on Apple M1 vs 4KB on x86 is one fingerprint axis.

Shared memory buffer. Combined with a Worker incrementing a counter, gives sub-microsecond timers that bypass `performance.now()` quantization — the canonical timing-attack primitive in browsers. Requires crossOriginIsolated.
Thread-blocking primitive. Used with SharedArrayBuffer for inter-Worker sync.
Wake threads waiting on Atomics.wait.
Atomic read from a SharedArrayBuffer. Heart of the busy-loop counter timer.
Atomic write to SharedArrayBuffer.
Atomic add. Counter-bump for SAB-timer worker.

console.log access. In legit code it's a print statement; in a detector blob the same expression often appears on the LEFT of an assignment (`console.log = trap`) to install an anti-logger that mutates a VM seed when an analyst tries to inspect internals. Look at adjacent assignment ops.

console.debug. Same anti-logger axis as console.log. Botguard variants prefer .debug because some loggers filter the channel — overriding it specifically catches conditional-logpoint users who think they're being quiet.
console.warn. Frequently overridden alongside log/debug in anti-logger setups.
console.error. DevTools formats Error objects synchronously, so wrapping .error gives the detector a hook to fire on uncaught exception logging — a clue that a debugger is attached.
console.info. Less frequently the anti-logger target but worth surfacing.

console.table. Synchronous DOM-style table render is a strong DevTools signal — Botguard-class blobs use it as a poor-man's `isDevToolsOpen()` (timing the call reveals whether a formatter is attached).
console.dir. Used to expand objects in DevTools; same anti-debug signal as console.table.
console.dirxml. Niche, but a few packers wrap this for symmetry with .dir.
console.trace. Reads the call stack — almost never legitimate in a fingerprinting detector; presence suggests it's being used to walk frames looking for puppeteer/playwright glue.

console.profile / profileEnd. DevTools-coupled performance API. Appearing inside detector logic strongly indicates an attempt to detect whether a profiler is attached (timing differences) or to confuse one (start a profile mid-VM to skew samples).
Companion to console.profile.
console.timeStamp. Drops a marker on the DevTools timeline. Same anti-profiler axis as console.profile.
console.assert. Sometimes wrapped to catch DevTools.
console.clear. Anti-analysis behavior: detector wipes the console after dumping debug data, so an analyst inspecting the log sees an empty buffer.
console.group / groupCollapsed / groupEnd. Almost always benign.
Same as console.group.
Same as console.group.
console.count.
console.countReset.
console.time / timeEnd. Pair forms an anti-debug timer when the delta is compared to a threshold (DevTools-attached formatters slow the call).
Companion to console.time.
console.timeLog.
Chrome-only `console.memory` getter (jsHeapSizeLimit etc.) — alternative entry to the performance.memory axis that some shims forget to spoof.
Bare console-global access. Almost always legitimate, but aliasing it to a local before overriding methods is a classic anti-logger setup; treat the alias + assignment pair as suspicious.
chrome.runtime.id. Undefined when read from a content-script context with no manifest match, populated when read from an extension page. Used to detect specific known extensions.

chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, message). Sending to a known extension's ID either returns a response or sets `chrome.runtime.lastError`; the response/no-response distinction reveals whether the extension is installed. Canonical Carnus probe.
chrome.runtime.connect(extensionId). Persistent-port variant of sendMessage; same installed-extension probe.
chrome.runtime.lastError. Set after a failing chrome.runtime.* call. Detectors read this after sendMessage to invert the probe (no error = extension exists).
chrome.runtime.getManifest. Only defined in an extension context; presence pins the script as running from an extension.
chrome.runtime.getURL. Resolves a chrome-extension:// URL — used by content scripts to load packaged resources.
chrome.webstore. Removed from Chrome in 2018; presence on a UA claiming a modern Chrome is a spoof tell.
chrome.app (chrome.app.isInstalled / chrome.app.getDetails). Vestigial after Chrome App deprecation, but a few packers still probe for it.

StyleSheet.cssRules. Iterating these on every stylesheet pre/post a known extension's load detects rule injection. Pair with document.styleSheets enumeration for the full Fingerprinting-in-Style (2021) probe.
CSSStyleSheet.ownerNode. Returns the <style>/<link> element backing the sheet — extension-injected sheets often have unusual owners (or none).
